text: Structured results include requested and actual dimensions, effective provider size when available, MIME type, and any resize/crop operation.
A mismatch yields an actionable warning in human output and a machine-readable status in JSON.
Document provider-specific size support and behavior for unsupported requests; an optional strict mode fails rather than silently accepting a mismatch.
Tests cover exact matches, mismatches, auto size, unsupported requests, and separation of native versus exported dimensions.
Reproduce child creation from an active agent session under the all-tools profile; test named and automatically assigned IDs against the documented schema.
Determine whether failure comes from invocation validation, session creation, environment inheritance, provider startup, or unsupported execution mode.
Supported creation returns a durable child ID and working inspect/message/lifecycle operations.
Invalid or unsupported calls return a stable error code and actionable explanation, including the valid invocation or supported fallback.
Add regression tests for the identified failure and negative-path diagnostics; ensure errors do not expose credentials.
Submission returns a job ID and persisted metadata/log locations immediately.
Status and wait expose queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled states, exit/error information, and artifact paths in structured output.
Jobs remain inspectable after the submitting CLI exits; interrupted jobs receive an explicit state rather than appearing to run forever.
Cancellation cleans up owned child processes without affecting unrelated work.
Batch execution supports bounded concurrency, per-item results, and retrying selected failures without regenerating successes.
Tests cover mixed outcomes, cancellation, interrupted submitters, concurrency limits, and output-path collisions.
Exact output dimensions can be requested with an explicit aspect-ratio policy and crop alignment.
Native generated originals are retained separately; overwrite behavior is explicit and safe.
Metadata records source dimensions, target dimensions, scaling/cropping, and source artifact linkage.
Exported/upscaled files are never presented as native-resolution generations.
Contact sheets support multiple artifacts with optional labels and deterministic ordering.
Tests verify dimensions, aspect-ratio handling, preservation of originals, missing dependencies, and partial export failures.
A successful generation can explicitly attach a preview for the agent's next visual review, using the shared attachment mechanism.
Metadata-only behavior remains available for scripts and non-vision backends.
Results identify the full-resolution artifact and any downsampled preview separately.
Unsupported vision/transport modes give clear fallback instructions without losing a successfully generated artifact.
Preview failures are distinguishable from generation failures; neither is silently interpreted as visual approval.
Tests cover attachment timing, capability gating, bounded payloads, and CLI/tool parity.
Record prompt, reference paths and content hashes, provider/model, quality, requested/effective/actual dimensions, timestamps, result status, and artifact paths.
Record seed or provider request ID only when actually supplied by the provider; do not fabricate unavailable metadata.
Edits and exports link to their source artifacts; manifests distinguish native outputs from derived copies.
Manifest writes are atomic, schema-versioned, and safe under parallel runs; failed operations retain useful diagnostic state.
A documented rerun/edit flow can consume recorded settings, with explicit overrides and clear warnings for missing references.
Do not persist credentials; document prompt/reference privacy and provide control over manifest persistence.
Tests cover round trips, lineage, moved/missing inputs, concurrent writes, and failed generation.
Jobs are usable through shell CLI and native agent tools with equivalent permission, state and cancellation semantics.
Ask and image job lifecycles remain distinct, and existing ask --events=jsonl retains the #66 canonical event contract rather than being replaced by a job envelope.
Export and contact sheets are explicit operations; ordinary generation/editing never silently invokes post-processing.

The missing image-input capability prerequisite is implemented and tested: per-profile capability override, advertised/executable tool gating and pre-turn image refusal, without duplicating the existing attachment transport.
Subsequent image edits can reference an earlier artifact or job, with explicit file paths retained, source-hash validation and actionable missing-reference behavior.
